report:
### Evidence Overview

Clinical research supports your skepticism: there is **no strong or consistent scientific evidence** demonstrating that hypnosis is an effective standalone treatment for smoking cessation. 

Key findings from the scientific literature include:

* **Methodological Limitations:** Evaluated studies on hypnotherapy for smoking cessation often suffer from significant methodological flaws, meaning its efficacy cannot be considered sufficiently proven ([PMC Study](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10929270/)).
* **Inconsistent Results in Reviews:** Meta-analyses and Cochrane reviews comparing hypnosis to control groups report mostly non-significant outcomes, with very few evaluated effects showing meaningful statistical significance over control interventions ([Frontiers in Psychology](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/psychology/articles/10.3389/fpsyg.2023.1330238/full)).
* **Uncertain Efficacy:** While hypnosis might offer complementary support for some individuals when paired with proven behavioral interventions, high-quality evidence is still required to confirm any independent benefit ([Healthline](https://www.healthline.com/health/hypnosis-to-quit-smoking)).

### Conclusion

Hypnosis is not supported by conclusive scientific proof as a primary method for quitting smoking. Standard medical and behavioral interventions remain the evidence-based recommendation.
